name: Unit 4 Test: Ch7 Sets & Counting, Ch8 Probability

coverage_spec: 7.1 Sets — De Morgan verification using cardinalities
7.3 Permutations — race finish orders with first-place restrictions
7.5 Combinations — committees with required-member constraints (lock-in trick)
8.1 Sample Spaces and Probability — colored-ball urn: sample size, P(color), complement
8.2 Addition Rule — chained: naive sum, addition rule, complement
8.2 Addition + Mutually Exclusive — 2×2 movie-genre table: joint, union, mutex check
8.2 Addition Rule Formula — given P(A), P(B), P(A∩B): P(A∪B), P(A and not B), P(neither)
8.4 Conditional Probability — medical-test Bayes chain: P(D∩+), P(+), P(D|+)
8.4 Conditional Probability — 2×2 STEM/year table: marginal + asymmetric conditionals
8.4 Conditional via Reduced Sample Space — two dice given sum=k: |reduced SS|, P(first=v|sum=k), P(first odd|sum=k)

mom_settings.intro:
Test Instructions

This is a graded individual test. Work on your own.

  • 3 attempts per question. A perfect first attempt locks in full credit; any subsequent attempt reduces the question's value by 33%.
  • Solutions appear after your final attempt within the date window.
  • 10 questions, 10 points each (100 points total).

planning_notes.selection_priority: All 10 questions are full multipart auto-graded (every part exercises a step of the chapter's processes — no single-step drills). Aligned with the Unit 4 Quiz (group test) principles: no FRQs, all multipart, every numeric answer accepts both decimal and fraction entry via $abstolerance = 0.005 on the number type. Coverage spans 7.1 (sets), 7.3/7.5 (counting), 8.1 (sample spaces), 8.2 ×3 (addition rule angles), 8.4 ×3 (conditional probability angles). 2026-05-11 revision: replaced the 2 FRQs (q9 Perm vs Comb, q10 2x2 Interpretation) with 2 auto-graded library questions (1824651 Addition Rule Formula, 1824664 Conditional via Reduced Sample Space) to match the group test pattern.

answer_format_note: Every number-type part uses $abstolerance = 0.005 per the probability/sets family conventions, so students may enter probabilities as exact fractions (e.g., 1/13) OR rounded decimals (e.g., 0.0769) interchangeably. IMathAS evaluates the entered expression and matches against the precomputed answer within tolerance.
